answer: Hand each applicant one jade transducer tuned to a single shale core drilled for that holder. The holder fires a pulse through the core and files the ripple arrival times; the registry checks it, then releases the next pulse deeper, so pulses run one after another and one core belongs to no second holder. A forged filing fails: no two cores share a strata fingerprint, so a replayed ripple never equals a fresh reading. One core costs $430 to drill and tune plus 22 lab hours; a farm chasing 5,000 fakes must drill 5,000 separate cores, $2.15 million and 110,000 hours; no quarry repeats a strata.
